title: RED oracle: two concurrent mutators serialize on the shared state_reconcile.lock; slow op holds it but NOT git_commit.lock
acceptance_criteria: ONE new pytest oracle file tests/harness/test_state_reconcile_lock.py is authored and touches no source.
Test imports state_reconcile_lock from harness.state_reconciler and is RED on HEAD because that module does not yet exist.
A two-mutator concurrency test proves both mutators NEVER enter the destructive section at the same time (mutual exclusion under the single shared state_reconcile.lock).
A test proves the slow destructive section runs while the dedicated state_reconcile.lock at state_dir/control/autowork/state_reconcile.lock is held.
A test proves git_commit.lock is NOT held across the slow section (a probe can flock state_dir/control/autowork/git_commit.lock while the slow op runs under state_reconcile_lock).
Every test is hermetic: builds its own tmp_path state_dir, never touches live state/, never opens the network.

spec.objective: Author the RED oracle that pins the shared-mutex contract for the not-yet-existing harness.state_reconciler.state_reconcile_lock: two concurrent mutators serialize on ONE dedicated state_reconcile.lock so they never both enter the destructive section, and the slow op is held under state_reconcile_lock but NEVER under git_commit.lock.
functional_requirements: Author exactly one new pytest file tests/harness/test_state_reconcile_lock.py that imports state_reconcile_lock from harness.state_reconciler; it is RED on HEAD because that module/symbol does not exist yet (import/attribute failure is the expected RED).

A mutual-exclusion test launches two concurrent mutators (threads) that each `with state_reconcile_lock(state_dir):` then enter a shared destructive section guarded by an instrumented counter, and asserts the observed max concurrency in the destructive section is exactly 1 (the two never overlap).

A test asserts that while a mutator holds state_reconcile_lock and runs a deliberately slow destructive op, the dedicated lock file state_dir/control/autowork/state_reconcile.lock exists and is exclusively held (a non-blocking flock attempt from a probe fails).

A test asserts the slow section never holds git_commit.lock: while the mutator runs its slow op under state_reconcile_lock, a probe CAN non-blockingly flock state_dir/control/autowork/git_commit.lock, proving git_commit.lock is distinct and not held across the slow op.
spec.interfaces: Drives the to-be-built context manager state_reconcile_lock(state_dir) from harness.state_reconciler; the lock file is the single dedicated state_dir/control/autowork/state_reconcile.lock, distinct from state_dir/control/autowork/git_commit.lock.
edge_cases: Module/symbol absent on HEAD -> import or AttributeError surfaces as the expected RED, not as a collection error that hides the assertion intent.
Concurrency instrumentation must use a real synchronization barrier so a non-serializing (buggy) implementation reliably trips the max-concurrency==1 assertion rather than passing by luck of timing.
fcntl may be unavailable on the platform; the probe assertions are written so the test only asserts the flock-based exclusion when fcntl is importable, skipping cleanly otherwise.
Every assertion operates inside its own tmp_path so re-runs and parallel test sessions never collide on a shared lock file.
non_goals: integration: NO live-daemon run; this is a hermetic two-mutator unit drive in its own tmp_path with no live state/ and no network.
Does NOT edit harness/state_reconciler.py or tools/brief_reaper.py (the impl task owns those).
Does NOT exercise classify_product, discriminators, cleanup_state, disk reapers, prepare_workspace, or any status logic — only the lock primitive's serialization contract.
Does NOT raw-edit or assert against any semantic marker (pause/full_stop/inactivity_escalated.json/live allowlist) and never raw-edits git_commit.lock.
spec.implementation_notes: Place the file at tests/harness/test_state_reconcile_lock.py (tests/harness/ already has __init__.py). Use threading plus a shared in-section counter protected so the test can observe overlap; gate exclusion via state_reconcile_lock around the section. For the lock-held / git_commit-not-held probes, open the lock files with os.open(O_RDWR|O_CREAT) and attempt fcntl.flock(LOCK_NB|LOCK_EX) from a separate fd, mirroring harness.autowork_daemon._acquire_commit_lock_or_reclaim's lock-file location convention (state_dir/control/autowork/<name>.lock). The slow op should sleep long enough that the probe runs while the section is still active. RED on HEAD is correct and expected for a test_authoring oracle.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Per-test tmp_path state_dir with control/autowork/ created on demand; no live state/, no fixtures beyond stdlib threading/fcntl; no network.

token_budget_ratio.note: Pure test_authoring oracle: all budget is the RED concurrency/lock-distinction oracle; no production tokens.
